Over the last several years, Korea Aerospace Industries and Indonesian Aerospace have been developing the KF-X fighter project. South Korea intends to use this to replace its aging fleet of F-5 Fighters and later on its F-15 and F-16 Fighters. The fighter was given the official designation and name: F-33 Boramae. Many decisions and design elements have now been decided upon and the development of a prototype is set to begin in December. Lockheed Martin was selected as the main foreign contractor assisting the Asian companies in the design and eventual production of the new fighter. This lead to settling on the GE F414 based twin engine design and abandoning the European style canard design option.

The initial Block 1 deliveries will represent technology comparable to Saab's Gripen with a radar cross section similar to the F/A-18. Block 2 models will improve the stealth capabilities to be comparable to the F-117. This upgrade will also add internal weapon bays capable of carrying 4xAMRAAM medium range air-to-air missiles or 2xAMRAAMs and 2xJDAM. The Block 3 technologies are expected to further the stealth technologies to the level of 5th generation fighters with a cross section similar to the F-35.

Weapons used will be a mix of domestic and foreign sourced guns and missiles.

F-33 Specifications  
Crew 1 (F-33A) or 2 (F-33B)
Length 15.6 m
Wingspan 10.7 m
Height 4.5 m
Powerplant 2 x General Electric F414-GE400K/EPE
Dry Thrust 13,000~13,500 lbf
Thrust With Afterburner 20,250~22,000 lbf
Maximum Speed Mach 1.97
Avionics AESA Radar
Datalink Capabilities
Infra-red search and track (IRST)
E/O Targeting System (EOTS)
Armament  
Gun 1xDaewoo 25 mm 4-barrel Gatling gun, internally mounted with 180 rounds
Hardpoints External: 6 Total (2xWingtip, 4 Underwing)
Internal (≥Bk 2): 4 Total (Air Combat: 4xAMRAAM, Air/Ground combat: 2xAMRAAM, 2xJDAM)

Production of a prototype will begin in April 2021. The first production plane is expected to have its first flight mid 2026. With delivery of the initial 120 jets by 2032. Indonesian Aerospace is expected to domestically produce their initial delivery of 80 jets over the same time frame.
